Multiplication of Single Digits

What You’ll Learn

Section titled “What You’ll Learn”

Multiplication is just repeated addition, and once you get comfortable with single-digit multiplication (the times tables), everything from multi-digit multiplication to algebra gets easier.

What Multiplication Means

Section titled “What Multiplication Means”

3×43 \times 43×4 means “3 groups of 4” or equivalently “add 4 three times”:

3×4=4+4+4=123 \times 4 = 4 + 4 + 4 = 123×4=4+4+4=12

The ×\times× sign means “groups of.” You can also read it as “times.”

Key ideas:

  • Order doesn’t matter: 3×4=4×3=123 \times 4 = 4 \times 3 = 123×4=4×3=12
  • Multiplying by 1 changes nothing: 7×1=77 \times 1 = 77×1=7
  • Multiplying by 0 always gives 0: 5×0=05 \times 0 = 05×0=0

Patterns That Help

Section titled “Patterns That Help”

The Full Times Table (1-12)

Section titled “The Full Times Table (1-12)”

Here’s the complete table. The green diagonal shows the perfect squares (a number times itself). Use this as a reference until the facts become second nature.

Notice the table is symmetric across the diagonal: 3×73 \times 73×7 and 7×37 \times 37×3 are both 21. That cuts the number of facts you need to memorize roughly in half.

The 2s: Just Double It

Section titled “The 2s: Just Double It”

2×2 \times2× anything is the same as adding the number to itself:

  • 2×3=62 \times 3 = 62×3=6 (double 3)
  • 2×7=142 \times 7 = 142×7=14 (double 7)
  • 2×9=182 \times 9 = 182×9=18 (double 9)

The 5s: Count by Fives

Section titled “The 5s: Count by Fives”

Results always end in 0 or 5:

  • 5×1=55 \times 1 = 55×1=5
  • 5×2=105 \times 2 = 105×2=10
  • 5×3=155 \times 3 = 155×3=15
  • 5×4=205 \times 4 = 205×4=20

The 9s Trick

Section titled “The 9s Trick”

The digits of any 9s product always add up to 9:

  • 9×2=189 \times 2 = 189×2=18 (1 + 8 = 9)
  • 9×3=279 \times 3 = 279×3=27 (2 + 7 = 9)
  • 9×4=369 \times 4 = 369×4=36 (3 + 6 = 9)
  • 9×7=639 \times 7 = 639×7=63 (6 + 3 = 9)

Also: the tens digit is always one less than what you’re multiplying by. 9×79 \times 79×7: tens digit is 6, ones digit is 3 (since 6 + 3 = 9). Answer: 63.

The 10s: Just Add a Zero

Section titled “The 10s: Just Add a Zero”
  • 10×3=3010 \times 3 = 3010×3=30
  • 10×7=7010 \times 7 = 7010×7=70

Squares (A Number Times Itself)

Section titled “Squares (A Number Times Itself)”

These come up constantly:

  • 1×1=11 \times 1 = 11×1=1
  • 2×2=42 \times 2 = 42×2=4
  • 3×3=93 \times 3 = 93×3=9
  • 4×4=164 \times 4 = 164×4=16
  • 5×5=255 \times 5 = 255×5=25
  • 6×6=366 \times 6 = 366×6=36
  • 7×7=497 \times 7 = 497×7=49
  • 8×8=648 \times 8 = 648×8=64
  • 9×9=819 \times 9 = 819×9=81

The Tough Ones

Section titled “The Tough Ones”

Most people find these the hardest to memorize:

  • 6×7=426 \times 7 = 426×7=42
  • 6×8=486 \times 8 = 486×8=48
  • 7×8=567 \times 8 = 567×8=56
  • 8×9=728 \times 9 = 728×9=72

A trick for 7×87 \times 87×8: “5, 6, 7, 8” → 56=7×856 = 7 \times 856=7×8.

Worked Examples

Section titled “Worked Examples”

6×96 \times 96×9

Use the 9s trick: tens digit = 5 (one less than 6), ones digit = 4 (since 5 + 4 = 9). Answer: 54.

8×78 \times 78×7

If you know 7×7=497 \times 7 = 497×7=49, then 8×7=49+7=568 \times 7 = 49 + 7 = 568×7=49+7=56.

4×84 \times 84×8

Double 8 twice: 2×8=162 \times 8 = 162×8=16, then 2×16=322 \times 16 = 322×16=32. So 4×8=324 \times 8 = 324×8=32.

Memorize the Times Tables

There’s no shortcut around it. Knowing your times tables cold makes everything from fractions to algebra dramatically easier. Drill them until they’re instant.
